notes: The San Francisco Call's weekly Real Estate and Financial Section for 1912, read page by page: the section's opening page and the pages that continued it (from April the section ran three pages - the city page, a country-land page and the improvement-club column), 131 OCR pages over 50 Saturdays, 6 January to 14 December. The three batches hold no issue after 15 December 1912. 1912 is after the 1909 renumbering, so the section prints today's numbers and every entry carries extra.record_date. Taken: numbered addresses where the section says something about the building itself - its storeys and material, its name, its use (hotel, lodging house, apartment house, hall), a firm that occupied it, a sale with its form and price, an auction offering with its lot - and the building-news column's new construction with its architect, which the section locates by corner rather than by number. Left out at extraction: sellers, buyers, lessors and lessees who are private people, estates named for them, and the buyers in the Ingleside Terraces sales lists.

coverage.remaining: The rest of the 1912 paper - about 9,500 OCR pages across curiv_angwin_ver02, curiv_calipatria_ver03 and curiv_dardanelle_ver01, where the fires, the building-permit lists and the news reports sit - is on disk but unread for this batch. The section for 21 and 28 December 1912 is in none of the three batches. 1913 (curiv_dardanelle_ver01, 15 issues; curiv_grimes_ver01, 132) is the next year of the same section.
coverage.note: 761 numbered-address mentions on the 131 section pages. 295 of them are repeats of an advertiser's own office - steamship agents, land companies, real-estate firms, the German Savings and Loan Society's branch list - and were read once each and not taken; about 30 more are out of town (Oakland, Stockton, Berkeley, a prize list of readers' home addresses). The remaining ~430, merged into 356 passages, were read one by one, and the building-news column was read again for every architect and contractor it names, which found the constructions it locates only by corner. Not taken: bare leases of a store, flat or dwelling between private people that say nothing about the building (about 90), meetings held at what reads as a private house, sales of 'lot and improvements' that name no building, numbers the OCR destroyed (S6 Mullen, SIOS Clay, 9.12 Folsom, 10r,5 Ocean, 0f.4 Baker and others), and real-estate firms moving between offices. 126 findings; 27 of them are buildings the section locates by corner or by name rather than by number.
